### THREAD 1 — buildDisImageSrc.ts / resolveDisImageSrc URL templating

Full source, `overrides/app/utils/buildDisImageSrc.ts`:
```ts
export const buildDisImageSrc = (url: string, quality = 80): string => {
  if (url.startsWith('data:') || url.startsWith('blob:')) return url;
  const separator = url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?';
  return `${url}[${separator}sw={width}&q=${quality}]`;
};

export const resolveDisImageSrc = (templatedSrc: string, width: number): string =>
  templatedSrc.replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g, '$1').replace(/\{[^}]+\}/g, String(width));
```
Confirmed call sites (verify these are the ONLY call sites, including test/story files):
- `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:94` — `src={buildDisImageSrc(src, quality)}` where `src` is `item.src`/`item.posterSrc` (raw, straight from `ZimmGalleryMediaItem`, never pre-templated).
- `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:244` — `src={resolveDisImageSrc(buildDisImageSrc(thumbSrc, imageQuality), THUMBNAIL_REQUEST_WIDTH)}` where `thumbSrc` is `item.src`/`item.posterSrc` (also raw).

Tasks:
1. Confirm via full-repo grep that these really are the only two call sites of `buildDisImageSrc`, and that NEITHER ever receives an already-templated string (i.e. no double-templating bug exists TODAY). But also assess robustness/defensiveness: if a future caller (or a bug) ever passed an already-templated src back into `buildDisImageSrc`, trace exactly what string results (walk the string transformation by hand) — is the failure mode a silently-broken image URL, or something that throws?
2. `resolveDisImageSrc`'s regex `/\[([^\]]+)\]/g` matches everything between the FIRST `[` and the FIRST following `]`. If the raw `url` argument to `buildDisImageSrc` itself already contains a literal, unescaped `]` character anywhere (e.g. inside an encoded query-string value from the SFCC/DIS CDN) BEFORE the templating brackets are appended — would this regex mis-match and produce a truncated/wrong URL? Assess plausibility: do real SFCC product image URLs (check any fixture/mock data in the repo, e.g. in stories or test files for realistic URL shapes) ever contain a literal `]`?
3. Confirm the `quality`/`width` parameters are always static/product-config-derived numbers at every call site, never influenced by unsanitized user/URL input.
4. `data:`/`blob:` URLs are passed through unchanged (no templating) — confirm this early-return actually prevents `resolveDisImageSrc` from ever being called on a `data:`/`blob:` string too (check the thumbnail call site specifically — if `thumbSrc` were ever a `data:` URL, `buildDisImageSrc` returns it unchanged, then `resolveDisImageSrc`'s regex runs against it anyway — could a `data:` URL (base64 payload) ever coincidentally contain a `[...]`-shaped substring that the regex would corrupt?).

### THREAD 2 — ZimmGalleryOverlay focus-trap / dialog correctness

Full relevant source already read for you, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx`:
```tsx
import { Image, Modal, ModalContent, ModalOverlay, VisuallyHidden, chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
...
const { mounted } = useZimmModal({ isOpen, onClose });
...
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isOpen || !contentNode) return;
  contentNode.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', titleId);
}, [isOpen, contentNode]);
...
if (!mounted || media.length === 0) return null;
...
return (
  <Modal isOpen={isOpen} onClose={onClose} motionPreset="none" size="full">
    <ModalOverlay __css={styles.overlay} />
    <ModalContent ref={setContentNode} sx={styles.panel}>
      <VisuallyHidden as="h2" id={titleId}>{productName}</VisuallyHidden>
      ...
    </ModalContent>
  </Modal>
);
```
No `initialFocusRef`, `finalFocusRef`, `trapFocus`, `returnFocusOnClose`, `blockScrollOnMount`, or `autoFocus` props are passed anywhere in the file (confirm this yourself by reading the ENTIRE file, ~341 lines, don't just trust this excerpt).

Tasks:
1. Confirm Chakra's `Modal` defaults for `trapFocus` (default true — uses `react-focus-lock` internally) and `returnFocusOnClose` (default true — restores focus to whatever had focus when the modal opened) actually satisfy AC 22/23 with zero explicit configuration here. Check the installed Chakra version's Modal source (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/modal` or wherever it resolves) if you need to confirm actual defaults rather than assuming from general Chakra knowledge — versions can change defaults.
2. Confirm `ModalContent`'s default `role` is `"dialog"` (not `"alertdialog"`) satisfying AC 24, and that the manual `aria-labelledby` workaround (the `contentNode.setAttribute` effect, justified by a code comment claiming Chakra silently drops a plain `aria-labelledby` prop on this ModalContent usage) actually results in a rendered DOM node with both `role="dialog"` AND `aria-labelledby` pointing at a real, present `id="zimm-gallery-overlay-title"` element. Trace this claim — is there a test (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx`) that actually asserts the rendered DOM has both attributes together, or does the test suite only check one or the other, or neither?
3. Find where `ZimmGalleryOverlay` is actually opened from — the "View Gallery" trigger buttons live in `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx` (`onOpenGallery` prop, called via `onClick={onOpenGallery}` in multiple places) — trace up through `product-view/index.tsx` to see how `isOpen`/`onClose` state is actually managed for the overlay (is there a `useState` toggled by the button's own click handler, with NO explicit ref ever passed to Chakra's `finalFocusRef`?). If focus-restore relies purely on "whatever had focus when Modal's `isOpen` flipped true," is there any code path (e.g. a state update batched with something else, an intermediate re-render) where the DOM focus could have shifted away from the actual clicked button before Chakra's Modal captures it? Read `useZimmModal.ts` (`overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts`) in full — confirm it does ONLY SSR-safe mount-gating and doesn't itself touch focus in any way that could interact with Chakra's own focus capture timing.
4. AC13 "returns to previous scroll position on the PDP" — the code comment claims body-scroll-lock (Chakra's own `blockScrollOnMount` default behavior) satisfies this "since locking/unlocking overflow never moves window.scrollY." Sanity check this claim against Chakra's actual scroll-lock implementation (does it ever apply a `position: fixed` + top-offset technique to the body, which WOULD need explicit scroll-position restoration, vs a simpler `overflow: hidden` technique which wouldn't) — check the resolved Chakra package source if feasible.

### THREAD 3 — video-as-positional-slot-only

Confirmed: `ZimmGalleryVideoItem` type (`zimmMediaTile/index.tsx`) has ONLY `posterSrc: string` and `posterAlt: string` fields — no real video URL/source field exists at all. `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts` NEVER emits `kind: 'video'` (always `'photo'`), by explicit design (SFCC-188 blocked on content-modelling). Confirm via full-repo grep that NO other code path (any component, test, or story) ever assumes a video item has a real playable `.url`/`.src` beyond `posterSrc` — i.e. nothing would throw/crash reaching for an undefined field. Separately, note for the record (still worth reporting, not necessarily blocking): the play/pause/mute buttons in `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx` (~lines 130-141) currently toggle only inert local `useState` with no observable effect (no real `<video>` element ever rendered) — assess whether a control whose accessible name is "Play video" but produces no observable change is a WCAG 2.1 AA concern (AC 25) worth flagging, or is reasonably out-of-scope given SFCC-188 is explicitly documented as blocking real video data.

REPORT FORMAT: for every finding — `file:line`, one-sentence defect statement, concrete failure scenario, confidence (CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE), severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. End with "What I tried to falsify" and "What I could not verify" sections. Don't pad.

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-731 AC 19 — wraps a raw SFCC product-image URL into the templated "dynamic src" format
3	 * base SFCC's `getResponsivePictureAttributes`/`DynamicImage` expect (see
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/responsive-image.js`'s own `getSrc` doc comment):
5	 * a `[...]` segment containing a `{width}` placeholder that gets swapped in per breakpoint via
6	 * SFCC's Dynamic Imaging Service query params (`sw` = scale width, `q` = quality).
7	 *
8	 * Deliberately does not build the `<picture>`/`srcSet` logic itself — that already exists in
9	 * `DynamicImage` and shouldn't be duplicated. This is only the one SFCC-specific piece missing
10	 * from that generic utility: the actual DIS query string for a given image URL.
11	 *
12	 * `data:`/`blob:` URLs are returned unchanged, with no template wrapper — DIS server-side
13	 * resizing is meaningless for a URL that already *is* the image bytes (there's no server to ask),
14	 * and appending a query-string-shaped suffix to a base64 payload corrupts it outright (the
15	 * browser fails to decode it, `net::ERR_INVALID_URL`) rather than merely doing nothing useful.
16	 *
17	 * @param url - Raw SFCC image URL (`disBaseLink` or `link`), with or without existing query params.
18	 * @param quality - DIS `q` param (0-100). Defaults to 80 — user-confirmed as the right baseline
19	 *   for this brand's product photography (2026-09-05); 60, the base SFCC image-gallery
20	 *   component's own default, showed visible compression artifacts on fabric/detail shots.
21	 * @returns A templated src ready for `DynamicImage`'s `src` prop or base's `getSrc` helper.
22	 */
23	export const buildDisImageSrc = (url: string, quality = 80): string => {
24	  if (url.startsWith('data:') || url.startsWith('blob:')) return url;
25	  const separator = url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?';
26	  return `${url}[${separator}sw={width}&q=${quality}]`;
27	};
28	
29	/**
30	 * Resolves a `buildDisImageSrc` template to a single concrete URL at a given width — the
31	 * counterpart read side of the same `[...]`/`{width}` format, for a caller (e.g. a fixed-size
32	 * thumbnail) that needs one resolved src rather than `DynamicImage`'s full responsive
33	 * `<picture>`/`srcSet` treatment. A project-owned equivalent of base SFCC's own
34	 * `getSrc` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/responsive-image`), kept in-house so this
35	 * templated-src format has one owner instead of a cross-package import for two lines of regex
36	 * (CodeRabbit, PR #81).
37	 *
38	 * @param templatedSrc - Output of `buildDisImageSrc`, e.g. `https://x/img.jpg[?sw={width}&q=80]`.
39	 * @param width - Concrete pixel width to substitute for `{width}`.
40	 */
41	export const resolveDisImageSrc = (templatedSrc: string, width: number): string =>
42	  templatedSrc.replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g, '$1').replace(/\{[^}]+\}/g, String(width));
